Reason (R): Sectors of a pie diagram are usually arranged in order of size.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: The whole circle of 360 degrees represents the total. R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about thematic maps: dot, choropleth and isopleth maps:
I. Isohyets join places of equal temperature.
II. In a dot map, all dots are of the same size and each dot represents a fixed number.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: II only
items.markingKey: (b) I is incorrect: Isohyets join places of equal rainfall; isotherms join places of equal temperature. II is correct.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem: In the study of line graphs, bar diagrams and pie diagrams, the term 'compound bar diagram' refers to:
items.answer: A bar diagram in which a bar is divided into components to show parts of the total
items.markingKey: (b) 'compound bar diagram' means a bar diagram in which a bar is divided into components to show parts of the total.
options: A graph used to represent time-series data such as temperature, rainfall or population growth
A bar diagram in which a bar is divided into components to show parts of the total
A map in which areas such as districts or states are shaded according to the value of a variable
A circle divided into sectors, each proportional to the share of a component of the total

items.stem:
Read the following extract on general rules for drawing graphs, diagrams and maps and answer the questions that follow.
"The title, legend and direction are important parts of the design of a map or diagram. The scale should be neither too large nor too small for the data and the space available. Graphs and diagrams make data easier to understand and compare than tables."
(i) Which of these is a general rule for drawing graphs and diagrams? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'legend' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Graphs and diagrams are used to present data. (1)
items.answer: (i) Selecting a suitable method and scale (ii) The key on a graph, diagram or map that explains the colours, symbols and patterns used. (iii) They make complex data easy to understand and compare at a glance.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) Selecting a suitable method and scale (ii) The key on a graph, diagram or map that explains the colours, symbols and patterns used. (iii) They make complex data easy to understand and compare at a glance.

items.stem: The following statement about thematic maps: dot, choropleth and isopleth maps is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "In a dot map, dots of different sizes are used."
items.answer: All dots are of uniform size, each representing a fixed value.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (All dots are of uniform size, each representing a fixed value.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
items.answer: pie diagram – several variables on one graph
items.markingKey: (a) pie diagram – several variables on one graph is wrong: pie diagram goes with sectors of a circle.
options: pie diagram – several variables on one graph
line graph – time-series data
line and bar graph – climograph of temperature and rainfall
compound bar diagram – components of a total

items.stem: The following statement about general rules for drawing graphs, diagrams and maps is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Any scale can be used without considering the data."
items.answer: The scale must suit the range of data and the space available.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (The scale must suit the range of data and the space available.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about thematic maps: dot, choropleth and isopleth maps is correct?
items.answer: Interpolation is used to draw isopleths between points of known values.
items.markingKey: (b) The others are wrong: Isohyets join places of equal rainfall; isotherms join places of equal temperature. Isopleth maps suit continuous phenomena; choropleth maps suit data by administrative units. All dots are of uniform size, each representing a fixed value.
options: Choropleth maps are best for continuous phenomena like temperature.
Interpolation is used to draw isopleths between points of known values.
Isohyets join places of equal temperature.
In a dot map, dots of different sizes are used.

items.stem: The following statement about line graphs, bar diagrams and pie diagrams is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Bars of a bar diagram can be of different widths."
items.answer: Bars should be of equal width.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (Bars should be of equal width.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: Population density (persons per sq km) of six districts is: District A: 400; District B: 366; District C: 811; District D: 542; District E: 488; District F: 187. Group the districts into three equal classes for a choropleth map and state how each class will be shown.
items.answer: Range 187–811; class interval ≈ 209. Classes – 187–395 low (lightest shade): District B, District F; 396–604 medium: District A, District D, District E; 605–813 high (darkest shade): District C. Shades increase in darkness with value.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for class intervals, 1 for allocating districts, 1 for graded shading.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about general rules for drawing graphs, diagrams and maps is correct?
items.answer: Graphs and diagrams make data easier to understand and compare than tables.
items.markingKey: (b) The others are wrong: The title is essential and should indicate the area, period and subject. A legend explains colours and symbols; a north arrow shows direction. The scale must suit the range of data and the space available.
options: The title of a diagram is not necessary.
Graphs and diagrams make data easier to understand and compare than tables.
A legend is used to show the north direction.
Any scale can be used without considering the data.

items.stem: What is meant by 'thematic map' in the context of thematic maps: dot, choropleth and isopleth maps?
items.answer: A map that shows the distribution of a particular phenomenon such as population, rainfall or crops.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: thematic map correctly explained as a map that shows the distribution of a particular phenomenon such as population, rainfall or crops.

items.stem: In a pie diagram of land under crops totalling 600 hectares, cotton occupies 75 hectares. What angle should its segment have?
items.markingKey: (b) Angle = value ÷ total × 360 = 75 ÷ 600 × 360 = 45°.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about thematic maps: dot, choropleth and isopleth maps:
I. Choropleth maps show data relating to administrative units such as districts and states.
II. In a choropleth map, darker shades are used for higher values and lighter shades for lower values.
III. Interpolation is used to draw isopleths between points of known values.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: All of them
items.markingKey: (a) I is correct. II is correct. III is correct.
options: All of them
II only
I and III only
I only

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"Graphs and diagrams make data easier to understand and compare than tables. The source of data should be mentioned below the diagram. Selection of a suitable method of representation is the first rule of drawing graphs and diagrams. The scale should be neither too large nor too small for the data and the space available."
(i) Explain the term 'legend', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Graphs and diagrams are used to present data. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "The title of a diagram is not necessary." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (1)
items.answer: (i) The key on a graph, diagram or map that explains the colours, symbols and patterns used. (ii) They make complex data easy to understand and compare at a glance. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: The title is essential and should indicate the area, period and subject.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) The key on a graph, diagram or map that explains the colours, symbols and patterns used. (ii) They make complex data easy to understand and compare at a glance. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: The title is essential and should indicate the area, period and subject.

items.stem: A bar diagram uses a scale of 5 cm = 100 thousand tonnes. How long should the bar for 400 thousand tonnes be?
items.answer: 20 cm
options: 40 cm
80 cm
20 cm
4 cm

items.stem:
Assertion (A): A suitable scale must be chosen.
Reason (R): Line graphs are usually drawn to represent time-series data.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (b) Both statements are true, but R deals with a different point and does not explain A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which term describes the following? A circle divided into sectors, each proportional to the share of a component of the total.
items.answer: pie diagram
items.markingKey: (a) pie diagram: a circle divided into sectors, each proportional to the share of a component of the total.
options: pie diagram
isopleth map
compound bar diagram
legend

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Isopleths are drawn using interpolation.
Reason (R): Values are known only at certain points, and lines of equal value must be estimated between them.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both are true and R explains A: values are known only at certain points, and lines of equal value must be estimated between them.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
